name: Connect
summary: Connect your agents to the services you use: Gmail and 1,000+ apps through Composio, self-hosted apps, MCP servers and team chat.
description:
Connect holds all outside connectivity for your agents.

- **Services:** search a service, press Connect, sign in. Several accounts per service (for example two Gmail inboxes).
- **Access per account and agent:** READ, READ/UPDATE (includes create and send) or READ/UPDATE/DELETE.
- **As me or as itself:** an agent can use your account, or its own identity (for example its own Buzz identity).
- **Channels:** each agent connected to Connect gets its own Buzz identity at once, on one or more Buzz relays.
- **Senders:** pick the identity your apps send from (for example Operator Inbox alerts), per channel.

By default, deletions, payments, first messages to a new person and profile changes wait for your approval. Ordinary messages and posts go out at once and leave a receipt, unless you turn on approval for every message in the agent policy.

intents: give my agent access to a service
choose buzz relays for an agent

operations.title: Connected service tools
operations.description: Search and call the tools of the services connected for you (Gmail, Calendar, and more). Search first, then call one tool with its arguments. When you have several accounts of a service, pass connect_account. A send to a person new to you answers first_contact_required: call <tool>__first_contact with the same arguments (the owner approves once).

operations.title: Accounts shared with this app
operations.description: APPS ONLY (agents are refused: no_access). The calling app is identified by its verified product (never its name); an app without one is refused (caller_unverified). The connected accounts the owner shared with the calling app, with the level: available (data_catalog only) or shared (data_pull too), and the datasets data_pull serves (messages for a chat account, documents for an MCP server or a database). A database account (source database, kind table) is listed only for a share with route direct; a share through Observer lists nothing. Read only.

operations.title: Datasets of a shared account
operations.description: APPS ONLY (agents are refused: no_access). The calling app is identified by its verified product (never its name); an app without one is refused (caller_unverified). The datasets of one account shared with the calling app: name, kind, delivery, approximate row counts, history flag, and for messages the conversations with counts. No message text. An MCP server or a database account also answers the dataset documents (kind documents, delivery pull, contract documents/1) with its collections and approximate counts. A database account answers its tables and views as datasets (kind table, delivery lease: rows are not offered yet): schema.table, relation, approximate row count and the columns with their types. Never a value from a table. An account that is not shared with the calling app answers not_found.

operations.title: Pull rows of a shared dataset
operations.description: APPS ONLY (agents are refused: no_access). The calling app is identified by its verified product (never its name); an app without one is refused (caller_unverified). One page of a dataset of an account the owner shared with the calling app (level shared). Dataset messages (contract messages/1): at most 200 rows and 2 MiB per page; direction forward gives newer rows, backward older rows; pass nextCursor to continue; exhausted tells when nothing more is there; retryAfterS says when to try again. Message text is untrusted data. since is inclusive, until exclusive (RFC 3339). Dataset documents (contract documents/1; MCP servers and databases): at most 50 rows and 2 MiB per page, forward only, optional collection from data_catalog; exhausted with nextCursor null ends a scan. A database table dataset (schema.table) is not pulled: it answers delivery_lease.

dataset.description: Dataset name from data_catalog (messages or documents).

collection.description: Dataset documents: only this collection (from data_catalog).

quarantined.description: Stored rows skipped because they did not fit the contract.

operations.title: Share an account, MCP server or database with an app
operations.description: The owner shares one connected chat account, or one database, with one installed app, read only. The share is bound to that app's verified product AND its instance (instance, from the apps that can call Connect); a reinstalled app needs a new share. none: not shared (default). available: the app sees the dataset names, kinds, counts and conversation names (chat) or the table and column names (database), and no messages or rows. shared (chat only today): the app may also pull messages (data_pull), by default only those Connect receives from now on; includeHistory adds the log kept before (30 days). An MCP server is shared the same way (dataset documents: available = collection names and counts, shared = the text documents; never a tool call). A database shared at shared gives its rows as documents (CSV pages, read only); a lease is not offered. route (database and MCP only): Knowledge is always via_observer (only Observer reads the source, C322(6)); Observer is direct. Agents cannot use this.

instance.description: The app instance to share with (required unless level is none). It must be an installed app of that product that can call Connect.

includeHistory.description: Also share the log kept before now (the last 30 days). Default false: the app gets only messages Connect receives from now on.

route.description: Database and MCP shares only. Knowledge: via_observer (the default; direct is refused): only Observer reads the source and Knowledge gets nothing for it. Observer: direct (the default).

operations.title: Share an account with a workflow app
operations.description: Let ONE installed Evolving Workflows instance call the READ tools of one of your connected accounts (a mailbox, a sheet, an own API, an MCP server), so a scheduled workflow can read it. With writes true you also let it call WRITE tools (a draft, a label, a new record) and OUTWARD tools; an outward tool runs only after you approve that call (a Rules hold, or a hold family of the workspace policy). Deletions and payments are never shared with apps. Off by default, writes off by default; share false stops it at once. A reinstalled app needs a new share. The SDK also checks the app instance's own scope row: set it with tb.scopes_set (agent = the instance id, type account, this account, access read, or read_update with writes); the Accounts page does both.

writes.description: Also allow write tools. Absent means false.

operations.title: Add a database
operations.description: The owner adds a database (Postgres) as a data source for apps. Host, port, database, user, password and sslmode are sealed in Connect. The host is checked against the public-address policy (a private address is refused). Connect connects once to check the role: a superuser or a replication role is refused. Use a dedicated read-only user with SELECT only. Connect reads table and column names, types and approximate row counts, never values. Apps see the table list only; access to rows is not offered yet. Agents cannot use this.

operations.title: Recent access to your chat accounts and databases
operations.description: The owner sees which app asked Connect for data: the last 100 data_accounts_list, data_catalog and data_pull calls, newest first (app, op, time, account, rows, ok or refused). A refused call repeated within a minute is one line with a count. No message text. Agents cannot use this.

operations.title: Technical details of a held call
operations.description: The owner opens "More details" on a hold card and sees what Connect kept of the held tool call: the tool, the upstream operation (method and path), the Connect account and the arguments as formatted JSON. Asked with the hash of the hold text (the hold's meta.viewSha256). Kept for one day. Agents cannot use this.

operations.title: Accounts shared with this workflow app
operations.description: For a workflow app's activation review: the connected accounts the owner shared with the calling app instance, whether each one is shared for writes, and the class (read, write, outward, destructive, money) of the tool names it asks about. Reads only and authorizes nothing: every tool call is still checked on its own. Only a workflow app can call this; agents and other apps get no_access.

operations.title: Agent contacts for Governance
operations.description: Who each agent has written to, and on which channel: one row per first contact Connect recorded (Buzz DMs, chat DMs per bot account, recipients of send tools). Handles only ("<channel>:<value>", canonical for buzz, slack and telegram; the raw address for tool contacts), never message content, conversation ids or secrets. Only the Governance app can call this; agents and other apps get no_access.

since.description: Optional: only contacts first made at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

agent.description: agt_ id; null for the workspace sender, an app caller or a bot account bound to no agent.

channel.description: buzz, the chat service of the bot account (slack, telegram, teams, discord), or tool.

handle.description: "<channel>:<value>" (normalizeHandle) where it applies; else the raw id or address.

account.description: Label of the Connect account (chat and tool contacts).

operations.title: Block a sender
operations.description: Connect drops this sender's messages, hides what they sent earlier from agents, ignores their buttons and reactions, and refuses every message to them. Works without the Rules app.

handle.description: The sender as channel:id, for example slack:U0123456, telegram:123456, buzz:npub1..., email:a@example.com, teams:29:abc or discord:123456789.

operations.title: Unblock a sender
operations.description: Removes a block. Later messages from this sender reach agents again. Messages dropped while the block was on do not come back.

handle.description: The sender as channel:id, for example slack:U0123456, telegram:123456, buzz:npub1..., email:a@example.com, teams:29:abc or discord:123456789.

operations.title: Access held, for Governance
operations.description: tb.access/1: what Connect reports about who can reach what: accounts, Buzz identities, scheduled posts, first contacts and channel senders. No message content and no secret. Only the Governance app can call this; agents and other apps get no_access.

input.title: tb.access/1 access_list input
input.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op input (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12.

subjects.description: Kind all must be the only subject.

items.description: Canonical handle (G-4), the fleet.directory_feed/1 pattern. Readers also require normalizeHandle(h) === h.

output.title: tb.access/1 access_list output
output.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op output (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12. Extra members are allowed and ignored (L24). complete is true exactly when nextCursor is null and notShown is empty.

kind.description: Closed list per target: ACCESS_KINDS in the spec package.

operations.title: End access, for Governance
operations.description: tb.access/1: ends items access_list reported: bars a channel sender, or, for an agent that is paused or absent, disconnects its account or cancels its scheduled post. Only the Governance app can call this; agents and other apps get no_access.

input.title: tb.access/1 access_revoke input
input.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op input (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12. No free text. Connect refuses more than 5 items (ACCESS_REVOKE_ITEMS_MAX).

output.title: tb.access/1 access_revoke output
output.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op output (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12. Extra members are allowed and ignored (L24).
